reason: Section 110 covers several distinct Crown Lands topics: notice and Recorder permission, Minister-required reclamation security, permanent structures and lessee consent, and timber-interest compensation with Board determination.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown Lands planned-work notice, Recorder permission and staking-survey exception
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(1) and 110(3) establish the notice and Recorder permission rule before damage or interference with Crown Lands and the exception for staking, grid lines and surveys.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Crown Lands notice and Recorder permission requirement and the staking, grid-line and survey exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reclamation program, security factors and approval before Crown Lands work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(2), 110(2.1) and 110(2.2) cover Minister-required reclamation programs and security, the factors for requiring them and the approval/security preconditions before work starts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when Crown Lands work may require a reclamation program and security and what must happen before work starts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Permanent structures and leased Crown Lands consent limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(4) and 110(5) separately restrict permanent camps or structures on Crown Lands and damage or interference with leased Crown Lands without lessee consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Crown Lands limits on permanent structures and on damage or interference with leased Crown Lands.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(6) and 110(7) address payment for timber cut or damaged, Board determination of disagreements and application of hearing provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how timber-interest payments and disputes are handled when mining rights affect Crown Lands timber.

reason: Section 111 is a focused security rule: security compensates owners or lessees for damage or interference and must be deposited before prospecting, mining or other work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Security for damage or interference before work on land
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 111(1) and 111(2) explain what security compensates and when it must be deposited with the Recorder.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what section 111 security compensates and when it must be deposited before work on land.

reason: Section 111.1 is one supplemental-security power allowing the Minister to require additional forms and amounts of security on top of security required elsewhere.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister power to require additional security

evidenceText: require security in the forms and amounts

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule authorizing additional security beyond environmental, section 111, other Act or regulation security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister’s power to require additional security beyond other security required under the Act or regulations.

reason: Section 111.2 separates how money security is credited and held in the Mine Reclamation Fund from the payment and refund purposes for which money may leave the Fund.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mine Reclamation Fund establishment, custody, account and interest
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 111.2(1) to 111.2(4) establish the Fund, identify eligible money security, assign custody, require a separate account and credit interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what money security is credited to the Mine Reclamation Fund and how the Fund is held and credited.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payments and refunds from the Mine Reclamation Fund
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 111.2(5) states the purposes for payments from the Fund: required protection, reclamation and rehabilitation work, and residual refunds with interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when payments may be made from the Mine Reclamation Fund for work or residual refunds.

reason: Section 112 gives one enforcement sequence for negotiable security: negotiate it after a non-payment certificate and require new security afterward.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Negotiating security after non-payment and replacing it
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address negotiating security to satisfy an unpaid amount and the following duty to deposit new security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when negotiable security is negotiated after non-payment and what replacement security is required.

reason: Section 112.01 is a definitions provision for the private-land acquisition Part, defining the key actors and terms used in vesting-order applications.

proposedGroups.reason: The target defines applicant, application, Court and owner for this Part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the defined terms applicant, application, Court and owner for private-land acquisition applications.

reason: Section 112.02 is one core rule making a Board vesting order the only recourse for a mineral claim holder needing private land and excluding the Expropriation Act compensation route.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Vesting order as only recourse for private land acquisition
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections establish that the Board decides whether private land should vest and determines compensation under this Part rather than the Expropriation Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall why a vesting order is the only recourse for acquiring required private land and what the Board determines.

reason: Section 112.03 is a focused application rule authorizing a mineral claim holder to apply for a vesting order when private land is required and agreement cannot be reached, with personal service on the owner.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application and owner service for vesting order
proposedGroups.reason: The current operative subsections state when the holder may apply to the Board and require personal service of the application on the owner.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a mineral claim holder may apply for a vesting order and how the owner must be served.

reason: Section 112.04 has one current operative rule: the Board sets and gives notice of the hearing date, time and place to the listed persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board notice of vesting-order hearing date, time and place
proposedGroups.reason: The only current operative subsection requires the Board to set the hearing and notify the applicant, owner, Recorder and interested persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must be notified when the Board sets the date, time and place for a vesting-order hearing.

reason: Section 112.05 identifies who may appear and be heard as interested persons in a private-land acquisition application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interested persons entitled to appear and be heard

evidenceText: interest under the Marital Property Act
right, title, interest, mortgage, judgment or lien

proposedGroups.reason: The target gives one entitlement to appear and be heard for persons claiming specified interests in the private land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which interested persons may appear and be heard in a private-land acquisition application.

reason: Section 112.06 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 112.07 is a single summary-hearing rule requiring written consent of the parties before the Board may hear and determine the application summarily.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Summary hearing with written party consent

evidenceText: with the written consent of the parties

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one Board power to hear and determine an application in a summary manner with written consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Board may hear and determine a vesting-order application in a summary manner.

reason: Section 112.08 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 112.09 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 112.1 gives one procedural rule allowing the Board to continue a hearing and make a determination in the absence of a party who received notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board hearing in absence of notified party

evidenceText: in the absence of that party

proposedGroups.reason: The target states a single rule about proceeding when a party had notice but is absent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Board may conduct a hearing and make a determination without a party present.

reason: Section 112.11 gives one timing-management rule allowing the Board to extend or abridge time fixed for anything in relation to an application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board extension and abridgement of application time
proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule about extending or abridging application-related time, including after expiry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Board’s power to extend or abridge time fixed for application steps.

reason: Section 112.12 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 112.13 separates the Board’s decision to dismiss or issue a vesting order from the required contents of a vesting order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board dismissal or vesting decision after hearing
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 112.13(1) states the grounds for dismissing an application and the alternative of vesting private land in fee simple.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Board may dismiss a vesting-order application or vest private land in the applicant.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required contents of a vesting order
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 112.13(2) lists the statements and provisions a vesting order must contain.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what statements and payment/proof provisions a vesting order must contain.
